convoLines.text: "Can I trust you? I mean really."
"That's the right answer. The wrong one would've been 'yes' too fast. That's the priority."
"I'll tell you what I tell everyone: watch what I do when nobody's watching. That's the whole of me. The rest is just talking."
"Still on whether they can trust you."
"I can't. Not today. Ask me when the work's done."
"Look, forget it. You wanted something?"
"Heinrich is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
You show them Black Walnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"I keep turning over the last thing Heinrich said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"The fire feels smaller without Heinrich. The rest of us will have to be bigger."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"What did you do for fun? Before. The thing you'd do on a perfect Saturday."
"I feel like — The free things. Turns out they were the expensive ones."
"I was a fisherman — fun was whatever I could steal between shifts. Now fun is watching the fire and not being afraid. It's a downgrade and an upgrade."
"Still on what you did for fun. You know?"
"It's nothing, really. What were you saying?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Heinrich owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"Sleep's gone strange. I taste the water before the others drink at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Ashanti grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Ashanti is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"Nobody says Heinrich's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
You show them Black Walnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"When's the last time you really laughed?"
"Stealing joy. I like that. We should steal more of it."
"Three days ago. Someone dropped a whole basket of tubers and we just stood there laughing. It wasn't even funny. It was the standing there. Just my read."
"Still on the last time you laughed. Not that it matters."
"Out there? I'd rather not die today, thanks."
"...Never mind me. What were you going to say?"
"I dreamed Heinrich was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
You show them Black Walnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"I should go. Before I overthink this conversation too."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Same time tomorrow, maybe."
"I've been turning something over. What do YOU think actually happened to us?"
"That's where I keep landing too. The question is what it wants."
"My theory changes weekly. This week's: we're the control group. Somewhere there's a village that got instructions, and we're the ones they just... watched. Cheerful thought, right?"
"Still on what you think happened to us. Could be wrong, though."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
Something crosses their face — quick, then gone. The practiced expression clicks back into place.
"I don't actually want to belong somewhere. I want to keep the peace. I keep my head down. Old habit. It kept me alive before; it keeps me alive now."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"You're really going to make me say it again?" Esteban rubs their face. "Fine — but it's the same truth as last time."
Esteban looks at you, level. "I told you the truth. You can keep poking it, but it's told."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Ashanti nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"See you around."
"About that question — Did you leave someone behind? ...Sorry. You don't have to answer that."
Just: "Yeah." A long quiet. "Me too."
The warmth pulls back a notch. They're weighing something.
"Still on who you left behind. Just... be straight with me."
"I'll keep it to myself. What's on your mind?"
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Since Heinrich died... I keep expecting to see Heinrich at the fire. Stupid."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Esteban nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"See you around."
"About that question — Do you believe in anything? Now, I mean. After everything."
"That's not naive. That's load-bearing. Hold onto it."
Their friendliness thins — still there, just held at arm's length.
"Still on what you believe in. But what do I know."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Last time things were different. They always are." "Heinrich always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Ashanti nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
You show them Elderberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You said yes — you left someone behind. I never asked who. I won't. But I'm still here, asking nothing, if that helps."
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
You walk to the tree line with Ashanti. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on that personal stuff."
They take it in and give nothing back. Not yet.
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "The Blood Tithe. They just... took Sofia. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Ruby nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"Sure. I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"We never did finish talking about what's been happening — that was 8 days back. Still on your mind? 'I should go. You know where to find me.'"
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
It's quiet at the hollow. Ruby doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on what's been happening."
They let the words sit there, unanswered.
"Okay, I'm all ears."
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You're family now. Chosen family — the kind that actually counts." "Make of that what you will."
"Here's what it would take, if you want more than this: show up when it costs you something. That's the whole test."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Ashanti nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"Sure. I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can I tell you something? At night I count the stars and name them after people."
"Thank you. I needed someone to know, and now someone does. Please keep it there."
"Me? Okay." "Listen. I need you to hear this before you go back out there."
"You've seen what's out there. I'm just saying — the treeline at dusk. Don't."
"Thank you. I needed to hear you say it."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Look, forget it. You wanted something?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "They took Sofia — The Blood Tithe, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"I should go. Before I overthink this conversation too."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

lines: d6: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d6: 🕯️ Heinrich Stepanov is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d6: What Heinrich kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d6: "Heinrich's gone." Ruby looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Heinrich." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d6: Grace picks up the journal. Their hands shake. Then they open it, and keep writing.

d6: 📖 LEARNED: Diplomatic Incident (Level 1). Trust builds 2x faster. You're TOO good though — once per week you can start a diplomatic incident: villagers argue, you pick the winner (+trust with them, -trust with the loser).
d6: 📖 LEARNED: Reading People (Level 1). Microexpressions leak truth. Watch the eyes, not the mouth. People tell you who they are.
d6: ⚡ TECHNIQUE UNLOCKED: Deep Read! You don't just read trust — you read intent. Know what they'll do next. (Your knowledge of Reading People amplifies your open_book.)
d6: 📖 LEARNED: Calming Panic (Level 1). Ground them: 5 things you see, 4 you hear, 3 you touch. Breathe with them. Slow is fast.
d6: 📖 LEARNED: Mediation (Level 1). Let each side talk without interruption. Repeat back what you heard. People de-escalate when heard.
d6: 📖 LEARNED: Keeping Morale (Level 1). People need small wins. Celebrate the little things. Despair is the real killer.
d6: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d6: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Heinrich Stepanov, 6 days. The mantle passes to Grace Obi.
d6: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Grace Obi, 43 — an ESL teacher. Her hands know different work now: Beast-calm.
d6: At the grave, Ruby, Ashanti speak for Grace — "Heinrich trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d6: The fire knew Grace before the Codex did — her name already carried weight here.

lastSay: d30: Ashanti spent the afternoon at the workbench and made 5 Crossbow bolt — and carries them now, their own work in their own hands.
d30: 🌿 Dandelion — the foragers have handled it 8 days running. They know it now — which parts are worth hauling, which bruise, how it wants to be carried. The village's knowledge deepens.
d30: 💡 Dandelion: the village knows more than you do. Harvest it a few more times (0/3) and it'll click.
d31: — DAY 31 DAWN — The world wakes. Animals are active.
d31: You wake with a start — something is wrong.
